hook.line: The number of possible chess games — far more than the atoms in the observable universe.
hook.say: Knighton here! Let’s tour 1,500 years of chess.

ch.say: In Persia, it was the game of kings.
p: Around the 6th century, India’s chaturanga became shatranj in Persia and spread through the Islamic world.
By about the 10th century it reached Europe through Spain and Italy, where its pieces turned into knights and bishops.

ch.say: The rules kept changing along the way.
tl: Chaturanga is said to arise in India
Shatranj spreads through the Islamic world
Reaches Europe via Iberia and Italy
In Spain the powerful queen appears — modern chess is born
First official world championship; Steinitz wins
IBM’s Deep Blue beats world champion Kasparov

ch.say: The old queen could only step one square diagonally!
p: In shatranj the queen’s ancestor, the fers, moved just one square diagonally.
In the late 15th century it became a queen that sweeps across the board — and the game got much faster.

cards: Chess’s ancestor, with short-moving vizier and elephants
An old-style chess still played in Thailand; pawns start on the third rank
The back rank is shuffled into one of 960 set-ups; proposed by Fischer

ch.say: Humans vs. machines made history too.
stats: A computer beats the world champion
cards: 12th-century pieces carved mostly from walrus ivory, found in Scotland in 1831
From Persian “shāh māt” — “the king is helpless”

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: No — until the late 15th century it was one of the weakest pieces
The king has no legal move but is not in check: a draw
Pawn 1, knight and bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9

p: Fifteen centuries after chaturanga, the next move is yours.
